conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I'll be your doctor during this stay. Can you tell me what brought you in today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, thanks. I’ve been having really bad stomach pain again—started a couple days ago. It started mild but got worse fast. I’ve been vomiting and can’t keep anything down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You have a history of chronic pancreatitis and Sjogren’s. Has this pain been similar to your usual episodes?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It feels like my usual pain, but maybe worse. I was doing well after my last hospitalization, but then my rheumatologist lowered my prednisone—from 10 mg to 5 mg—about five days ago.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And you think that might have triggered this flare?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Every time my prednisone drops, I tend to flare. I also noticed this rash on my arms—same as when my Sjogren’s acts up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s helpful. We’ll keep that in mind. For now, we’re going to start with IV fluids and pain control. We’ve ordered blood tests and an ultrasound to check your gallbladder and liver.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’m allergic to morphine, just so you know.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Thanks for reminding me. We’ll use Dilaudid instead, which we used safely last time. We’ll also give you an anti-nausea medication to help with the vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That sounds good. I just want to get through this episode.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi again. Your ultrasound results are back. Good news—it shows a normal gallbladder, no gallstones or sludge. Liver looks fine too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. So it’s not my gallbladder?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, it doesn’t look like it. Given your history, we think this is another flare of your chronic pancreatitis, possibly triggered by the prednisone taper.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. What about the rash?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The rash fits with your Sjogren’s flares. We don’t think it’s anything new or infectious. We’ll monitor it, but no specific treatment is needed right now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks. How long do you think I’ll need to stay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll reassess tomorrow. Right now, we’re focused on controlling your pain and nausea so you can start eating again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little better. The pain is still there, but not as intense. I haven’t vomited since yesterday evening.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s progress. We’re going to try advancing your diet to clear liquids today—if you tolerate that, we can move to soft foods tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. I’m ready to try something besides IV fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also got your urine culture back. It showed mixed bacteria, but it looks like contamination from skin or genital flora—nothing to treat.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. So no UTI?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, we don’t think so. The result suggests the sample wasn’t collected perfectly, but it’s not a real infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Should I be doing anything differently next time?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll give you instructions on clean-catch technique for future tests. But no worries this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just checking in. How’s the clear liquid diet going?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had some broth and apple juice. No nausea or pain so far.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s excellent. We’ll keep you on this for a few more hours, then try soft foods like toast or mashed potatoes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m feeling hopeful. Do you think I can go home tomorrow?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. If you keep improving, we could discharge you by tomorrow afternoon. We’ll need to make sure your pain is controlled with oral meds and you’re eating well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about my prednisone? Should I go back to 10 mg?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll discuss that with your rheumatologist. For now, we’ll keep you on 5 mg, but we’ll recommend a slower taper next time to avoid flares.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That would be better. I’ve been struggling with malabsorption too—need to take my enzymes regularly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll make sure you have a clear plan for pancreatic enzymes and diet. We’ll also send a note to your GI doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—you tolerated dinner last night and your pain is much better. We’re planning to discharge you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great to hear. What meds will I be on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll continue Dilaudid as needed for pain, anti-nausea meds if needed, and your regular pancreatic enzymes with meals. Keep taking prednisone 5 mg daily for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll schedule appointments with rheumatology and GI. Call us if the pain worsens or you start vomiting again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you so much. I feel much better already.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll get your discharge papers ready. Safe travels home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—should I watch for the rash?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, but it should fade as your Sjogren’s stabilizes. If it spreads or becomes painful, let your rheumatologist know.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’ll see you in follow-up soon.
